reason: Re-opened packet.js veda 84 --verse 8.39.4 (revision 275528, dated 2020-09-29 by the API): Sāyaṇa glosses śaṃ as śāntinimittam and yoḥ as viṣayayogajanitam, both as mayaḥ sukham, and closes yaḥ kaścanāpi devo yadi hūyate agnir eva sarvaṃ karoti; the evidence words are verbatim and carry both halves (delight as happiness from calm and from contact with sense objects; Agni doing all whatever god is invoked) without drift. Wilson’s note names the śānti/viṣaya gloss as Sāyaṇa’s, so it is not the translator’s. The earlier refutation’s objection (the refrain’s ‘others’ glossed as godless foes) no longer applies: the new context clause places the verse after 8.39.3 (the worshipper’s blissful messenger) and names its turn to Agni’s gifts, which day.js bears out, with no four-word run from the key. No school needed, no comparison, no hard passage. verse.js ok (8.39.4 at [658,4], ends at a sentence stop before the refrain); entry-check ok.
